summary.headline: Thermax Q1 FY27: INR 91 crore cost-to-completion hit on a legacy government EPC project, plus ~INR 300 crore of unshipped inventory, drove a weak quarter with revenue up only ~7%.
summary.overview: Management called Q1 FY27 the toughest quarter relative to expectations in recent years. The main drag was a INR 91 crore cost-to-completion charge on a legacy PSU/government project (original order ~INR 1,200 crore, taken in FY22), triggered by late engineering changes from the engineering partner in June. About INR 300 crore of finished goods, largely export shipments including Middle East, slipped out of the quarter due to high freight and customer deferrals, and commodity-linked cost increases of about INR 10 crore hit Industrial Products. Green Solutions lost about INR 20 crore at FEPL and carried about INR 8 crore of cost in Bio-CNG. Management reiterated that FY27 should be a good year, with the backlog (~INR 14,000 crore) and order inflow expected to exceed FY26, while acknowledging a credibility problem on execution and communication.

financial_highlights.change: Barely delivered 7% growth, including the effect of ~INR 300 crore of shipments that slipped
Loss-making project; loss accounted for in full up-front
Deferred from Q1 to Q2; partly shipped
In line with expectations per management
Not expected; includes Tamil Nadu project hold-ups and carrying costs of external investor process
Carrying cost of team with no new projects for two years
Management said this was achieved in Q1

segments.name: Industrial Infra / Projects (TBWES and legacy EPC)
segments.commentary: Legacy government/PSU projects (FGD, HRRL, NRL) carry the risk; the INR 91 crore hit relates to one PSU project with ~74% invoiced and ~26% balance. Management says all other projects >INR 100 crore net add to margin, and targets 10%+ profitability on the business.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Double-digit YoY growth in Q1 but profitability dipped on steel prices (plates up ~18%, INR 52-53 to INR 61+/kg in two months) and ~INR 300 crore of shipments deferred. Management expects Q2 margin pressure, with cooling backlog weighted to Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Volumes recovered and double-digit EBITDA was achieved in Q1. Management guides to at least 20% growth, with commodity and China-competition risks and a 10% US tariff as watch items.

segments.name: Green Solutions (TOESL, FEPL, Bio-CNG, Hydrogen)
segments.commentary: TOESL is running above INR 600 crore annualised and targets INR 800-1,000 crore over two years; booked its largest order of INR 120+ crore in the quarter. FEPL posted a INR 20 crore loss and an external investor is to take a substantial majority. Bio-CNG took an INR 8 crore quarterly carrying cost with no new projects for two years. Hydrogen has a team of 40-50 people and one handshake pending announcement.

guidance_outlook: FY27 is expected to be a good year; management says it expects to exceed FY26 order inflow, with the backlog to translate into revenue as legacy projects finish.
Q2 expected to be a good profitability quarter, helped by LD reversals and collections; Q2, Q3 and Q4 each to show significant YoY improvement, per management.
Management expects to ship over INR 3,000 crore per quarter; two to three quarters above that level this year would lift gross margin flow-through.
Industrial Infra targeted at 10%+ profitability once legacy projects are complete; the last legacy PSU exposure (~INR 300-400 crore) expected to close out, with NRL slipping into Q1 FY28.
FGD: one plant handed over in Q1, another due Q2 and the last in Q4 FY27. HRRL completed this quarter.
Bio-CNG: remaining PGTR tests in August and September; policy-driven tariff increase of 20-30% expected around August; pipeline expected in Q3-Q4.
Data centre cooling: management expects two more US cooling wins in Q3-Q4 (handshakes in Q1-Q2). A first US boiler/pressure parts shipment slips from Q2 to Q3 recognition.
Hydrogen: expects an announced order next quarter and revenue next year; SOEC demo plant to go up by end of FY27.
Kandla green methanol project (<INR 100 crore) execution expected Q4 FY27 to Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Adding capacity in TBWES (boilers and pressure parts) at its own plant and through its supplier ecosystem to meet a growing thermal pipeline.
Hydrogen SOEC demo plant to be commissioned at end of FY27 as a showcase plant, with a team of 40-50 people in engineering and setup.

FEPL platform to be majority-sold to an external investor during FY27; several Tamil Nadu renewable assets awaiting regulatory approval to start power generation, which management expects within a week.
Bio-CNG: two projects (~INR 250 crore) needed to absorb the current team and offset ~INR 8 crore per quarter cost.
demand_pricing: Order book is ~INR 14,000 crore; management expects FY27 order inflow to exceed FY26, but Q1 was muted because two handshake orders (a few hundred crore each) could not be booked without advances.
Pipeline: thermal (supercritical, subcritical, captive) is among the largest; Middle East and Africa (refining and petrochemicals) strong; US data centres in cooling, boilers and water.
Water: ZLD is now the largest part of the Water business. Air pollution control retrofits in northern India cited as opportunity.
Pricing pressure: steel prices up ~18% and crude and commodity volatility. Chemicals faces competition from Chinese exporters and a 10% US tariff.
Management says export and private projects are performing well; PSU/government projects are being stopped and repriced for risk.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the legacy project behind the INR 91 crore hit, and how much remains to execute?
qa_highlights.answer: Original order ~INR 1,200 crore taken in FY22; the loss on the project is ~INR 150 crore in total. About 74% is invoiced and 26% remains. The engineering partner has confirmed its engineering is 100% complete; execution is over the next four quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are government and PSU contracts a continuing risk, and do you have claims against the engineering partner?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the project a mistake and said the model (taking large PSU work with an outside engineering partner) will not be repeated. Government/PSU orders are now under INR 300-400 crore (<5% of backlog). They will only bid selectively where they have unique capability and can price the risk; one IOCL project (~INR 50-60 crore) and a Kandla green methanol project (<INR 100 crore) were cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company's execution and guidance credibility repeatedly weak, and is talent an issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the top five people on the project had 20+ years at Thermax, and that talent was not the root cause. It said that gross project execution across >INR 100 crore projects adds to margin outside this one project. It acknowledged that surprises should be communicated earlier, though it did not commit to pre-announcing profit warnings.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for order inflow and which segments drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 order inflow to exceed FY26. Drivers: a repeat supercritical project (at least one), Middle East and Africa international work, data centre cooling, waste-to-energy and captive thermal. Q1 handshakes worth a few hundred crore are pending advances.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 300 crore slipped revenue the right basis for estimating EBITDA uplift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins are not 45-50%; they range 15-30% for most businesses. Slipped export items carried above-average margins. The US data centre shipment slips to Q3 recognition, while Q2 will see LD reversals and collections, and a large scheduled Q2 shipment is already in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will policy changes drive a significant pipeline, and in which segments?
qa_highlights.answer: The only policy change referenced is for Bio-CNG: a 20-30% price increase and blending mandates are expected around August (possibly at an August 10 conference). Green methanol tenders by SECI are also a potential driver. Thermal and cooling growth are not policy-dependent.

risks_watch: Completion of the legacy PSU project over four quarters; further cost escalation beyond the provision (LD exposure partly reserved).
Q2 Industrial Products margin pressure from steel and commodity costs; whether the ~INR 300 crore deferred shipments are fully recognised in Q2-Q3.
Order inflow recovery: the handshake orders need advances to be booked; the data centre and thermal pipeline must convert.
Bio-CNG policy announcement (price increase of 20-30%) expected around August; PGTR outcomes for remaining two projects in August and September.
Credibility: repeated gaps between guidance and execution; management said it would share surprises earlier but did not commit to profit warnings.
Chemicals margins: commodity pass-through and US tariffs; FEPL external investor process and Tamil Nadu regulatory approvals.
summary.management_tone: Candid and self-critical on execution and disclosure, with an explicit acknowledgement that Q1 was the toughest quarter in years. Confident about FY27 orders, backlog conversion and Q2-Q4 profit recovery, but relies on promised policy, pipeline conversion and data-centre wins that are not yet booked; several answers were qualitative on margin and guidance.
key_quotes: A very difficult quarter, felt like was the toughest one, at least relative to expectations for the past few years that we have had, not that we haven't had tough quarters in the past, but this one felt particularly so.
And I would say even with taking this INR 91 crores hit, I expect this year to be a very good year.
So, I stay very bullish on orders and continuing to build a pipeline of the kind that we like and want to execute better on.
I think going forward, I'm not committing to it. It's between us as a team to decide, but I think this is something that we could have done.
It's not a quarter that we are proud of , nor is it reflective of what the company that we are building at Thermax and the performance that we can deliver at Thermax.
